acceptance.output_evidence:
THE READING, WITH NO VERDICT ON IT.
(1) WERE THE MERGES BY IDENTITY EVERYWHERE THEY CLAIM TO BE? Yes, and the census is the evidence rather than the assurance. Every merge required a stitch id to resolve to EXACTLY ONE canonical id under a stated rule -- the pipeline suffix after ':gold:', the S3 key after the bucket, a Component id verbatim, a query key with its quotes stripped. Where more than one canonical id matched, the member was CARRIED: 24 firm-relative S3 keys exist in two firms' buckets, and choosing one would have invented a cross-firm claim. 0 pipeline suffixes were ambiguous. The strongest check is external: three of the four resolution figures reproduce the CVO's own C-S40 census exactly, computed by a different seat with a different instrument.
(2) WHAT ARE THE 269 CARRIED MEMBERS? Two different things, and the reasons separate them. 175 are 'no canonical X' -- the projection's own extractors do not have the object at all: 68 query keys, 125 S3 keys, 50 pipeline members, 2 components. Some of those are REAL objects the canonical side misses (a gold script the pipeline extractor does not reach, an S3 key only the trace sees) and some are EXTRACTOR ARTEFACTS of the stitch side: 'rqk:QUERY_KEY' is a variable name, and several query keys are multi-line template expressions captured verbatim. Those are a producer gap on the STITCH side and belong in front of whoever owns cache_cli extraction. The remaining 24 are the ambiguity above, which is neither a gap nor an artefact but a genuine multi-firm object that a single id cannot name.
(3) DOES THE GRAIN SPLIT LEAVE ANY MIXED-GRAIN NODE? No node is left mixed: every GOLD_SCRIPT member is assigned by its own id shape -- exactly one ':' after 'gold:' is a file, two is a function -- so the 1,380 become 166 PipelineScript and 1,214 PipelineFunction with nothing straddling. What the split does NOT do is guarantee the canonical side agrees about which is which: 132 of 166 scripts and 1,198 of 1,214 functions resolve, and the 50 that do not keep the grain the stitch assigned them. If the canonical extractor would have called one of those 50 a function where the stitch calls it a file, nothing here would detect it -- the carry preserves the stitch's grain judgement unexamined, and that is the one place a grain claim in this cell rests on the producer rather than on a comparison.
(4) WHAT THE CVO NEEDS TO RE-SIGN THE MAP. 65 -> 61 keys; aws 34 -> 33, portal 18 -> 16, pipeline 4 -> 3, ms 7 and semctl 2 unchanged. THE FROZEN COND-A RESOURCE-TYPE COUNT IS UNMOVED AT 32: S3_DATA_KEY merged INTO S3Key, which was already an aws type, and no aws type was created or destroyed -- the aws LAYER count moves because a retired entry left it, not because a resource type did. PORTAL_BUNDLE stays as the one genuinely new class. The comment keeps the GO's own words and its re-sign line reads PENDING.
(5) AND THE THING THE CRITERION DID NOT ASK, WHICH IS NOW THE ORDER'S OUTCOME. The map is not the only certified carrier of this vocabulary. grain_baseline.json names all four retired types with certified counts, and AC-GRAIN.2 refuses on the zero they correctly become, so the producer cannot publish the unified artifact at all (W2-S60). The CVO's re-sign of the map and a recertification of those four baseline classes to 0 are the same decision seen from two files, and taking one without the other leaves the producer refusing.
